passage: The community hall was loud with a birthday party, and Uday sat on the mat with a bucket of blocks, frowning at his fallen towers. Then he noticed Rukmini, the neighbour, at the next mat, laying two long blocks side by side before adding more. Uday copied it, base first. His tower rose past every one he had built before. "It just stays up," he said, puzzled, and grinned.

qa.q: What did Rukmini do with the two long blocks?
qa.a: Rukmini laid two long blocks side by side before adding more.

qa.q: What was Uday feeling when the tower rose past his earlier ones?
qa.a: Uday was pleased and a bit puzzled, since he grinned but could only say "It just stays up."

qa.q: What alternative could help Uday, and why?
qa.a: Uday could ask Rukmini why the base matters or test a wide and a narrow base himself, because understanding the reason would help him build well with any blocks.

qa.q: How might Rukmini see Uday copying the base?
qa.a: Rukmini may not have noticed at all in a loud hall, or may be flattered; either way the base works and Uday's tower is proof.

grounding: A boy copies a neighbour's wide base of two long blocks and builds higher than before without being able to explain why.
